notes: Same access pass as Bestsellers/New Arrivals: direct HTTP GET, no block, robots.txt clean. Investigated Article's Sale-related nav thoroughly because the prior Furniture pass flagged Article as known for a 'Sale' section. Found TWO distinct sale-family nav entries: (1) id='shop-all-sale' -> /c/shop-sale, currently labelled 'Shop All Labor Day Sale' - this is a generic rotating seasonal promo (page is themed 'Labor Day', headline banner, room-by-room sale tiles like /c/shop-sale-living-room, /c/shop-sale-bedroom etc; its own on-page 'Sale' filter shows 'Current Sale (178)' vs only 'Clearance Sale (1)' - i.e. almost entirely non-clearance stock) - EXCLUDED as a generic Sale page per the brief's Sale-vs-Clearance test, no row emitted. (2) id='clearance-sale' -> /c/sale, which the site's OWN main-nav literally labels 'Shop Clearance' - this is the strongest taxonomy signal on the site. Opened /c/sale directly: canonical URL https://www.article.com/c/sale, H1 'Here's the deal.', breadcrumbTitle 'All sale', current banner also themed 'Labor Day' (same seasonal creative reused), and the underlying Contentful block is literally named 'sale-clearance-product-grid' with saleFilter 'Sale & Clearance Products' - i.e. this single URL merges ordinary Sale stock and true Clearance stock together, it is not a clearance-only listing. However, individual product records on this page carry two independent booleans, onSale and onClearance, and the page's own 'Sale' filter group exposes two mutually-labelled facet options with exact site-reported counts: 'Current Sale (178)' and 'Clearance Sale (107)' - a genuine, deliberate clearance/non-clearance split in the site's own taxonomy, not something I inferred. There is no separate canonical URL for the clearance-only subset (no query-string or path variant found; the filter is client-side and the canonical tag on /c/sale points back to /c/sale itself), so I could not verify a clearance-only page load independently the way I could for a normal PLP. Recording it as a row against the /c/sale URL with the exact facet-reported qty of 107, flagged for manual review because it is a filtered subset of a combined, seasonally-themed Sale page rather than a standalone dedicated Clearance URL - genuinely uncertain per the brief's own guidance, better to record with evidence than guess either way. No other clearance/outlet/final-sale/last-chance/end-of-line wording was found anywhere in category_sitemap.xml, collection_sitemap.xml, landingpage_sitemap.xml, tag_sitemap.xml, or the 221-entry nav tree (an 'outlet' text hit in the raw HTML was a false positive - Vue's '<!--ssr-outlet-->' template comment, not site content). Did not use site search (/search?*) - robots.txt disallows it and nav discovery already positively surfaced the clearance-labelled nav entry, satisfying the absence-proof requirement in the affirmative direction.

rows.evidence: Main nav labels this URL 'Shop Clearance' (id=clearance-sale). On-page 'Sale' filter group at /c/sale shows facet option aria-label 'Clearance Sale (107)', distinct from sibling facet 'Current Sale (178)'; individual product JSON on the page also carries an independent onClearance boolean (e.g. onSale:false, onClearance:true) separate from onSale.
rows.flag: MANUAL REVIEW: AMBIGUOUS SALE/CLEARANCE - /c/sale is nav-labelled 'Shop Clearance' and has a genuine site-taxonomy 'Clearance Sale' facet distinct from 'Current Sale', but the page itself (H1 'Here's the deal.', breadcrumbTitle 'All sale') is a combined 'Sale & Clearance Products' grid currently re-themed as a Labor Day seasonal promotion, not a dedicated standalone Clearance URL - qty 107 is the site's own facet count for the Clearance-tagged subset of this combined listing, no separate clearance-only URL exists to verify independently.
